Read the whole file to understand the pattern, even though you are NOT overriding this file or importing from it. 4. `overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` — Tier 2, import and use it, do NOT modify it. This is how you'll derive which image is currently in view for the touch/indicator path. ## Design source (verified Figma — do not re-derive) - `Image Group` component set, node `40002742:46323` — 4 size variants (Large 288×432, Hero 288×436, 5:4 1056×1320, Small 179×268). The "Large" variant (`40002742:46322`) contains: `imageContainer` (full-bleed image), a `Tag` overlay top-left (78×48, the badge slot), a `Close` overlay top-right (48×48, the remove-CTA slot, wishlist only), and a `Carousel` overlay (288×24, vertically centred, two 24×24 `touchContainer` arrow buttons at x=12 and x=252). The "Small"/mobile variant (`40002742:46321`) has the same `imageContainer`/`Tag`/`Close` but NO `Carousel` — instead a `Slide-indicator` instance flush to the image's bottom edge. - This means: **arrows only on desktop/hover-capable pointers, the slide indicator only on touch — never both, per the resolved decision recorded in the plan (§4a) and confirmed directly in the Figma structure itself** (Large has Carousel+no-indicator, Small has indicator+no-Carousel). - Touch paging is native CSS scroll-snap on every breakpoint — see plan §4b: one scroll container always, `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` + `scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` per slide; arrows call `scrollBy()`/`scrollTo()` as progressive enhancement over the same container; the indicator's active index derives from `useIntersectionObserver` watching which slide is most visible (or a `scrollend` listener — your choice, either satisfies the pass criteria). ## Component contract Props: ```ts type ZimmProductCardMediaImage = { src: string; alt: string }; type ZimmProductCardMediaProps = { primaryImage: ZimmProductCardMediaImage; hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardMediaImage; images?: ZimmProductCardMediaImage[]; swapOnHover: boolean; showControls: boolean; badge?: React.ReactNode; onRemove?: () => void; removeLabel?: string; // accessible name for the remove button, e.g. product name — required if onRemove is passed; use your judgement on how to type this relationship (a discriminated union isn't necessary here, this is a simple co-requirement, document it in a JSDoc comment and defensively no-op if onRemove is passed without a usable label) priority?: boolean; // LCP escape hatch for the primary image }; ``` Holds the current paging index in local `useState` (a single piece of state — below this codebase's extract-to-hook threshold per `.claude/rules/components.md`). Stamp `data-card-slot` attributes on the root and/or key sub-elements (e.g. `data-card-slot="media"`, `data-card-slot="tag"`, `data-card-slot="close"`, `data-card-slot="carousel"`) so a LATER step (the organism, Step 6) can select these descendants from its own recipe for hover-reveal — you are not implementing hover-reveal CSS in THIS component's own recipe (that's explicitly the organism's job per the plan), just exposing stable selector hooks. Pick attribute names and values that are self-evidently stable identifiers, not implementation details — document the contract in a one-line comment at the top of the file so Step 6 knows what to select. ## Behaviour and exact pass criteria **AC1 (highest priority) — primary image renders in every configuration.** With `hoverImage`, `images`, and `showControls` ALL absent/false, the primary image must still render. Test this across all 6 variation×unavailable combinations is actually the ORGANISM's job in Step 6 — for THIS component's own test, just prove it holds with minimal props (only `primaryImage` + required `swapOnHover`/`showControls` booleans set to false). **Images:** - Every `` (there may be several — primary + hover + gallery images) has a real, non-empty `alt`. If `alt=""` is ever used for a genuinely decorative image, that needs a justifying comment — but in this component every image IS the product photo, so every `alt` should be meaningful (typically the product name, passed in via each image object's own `alt`). - Non-primary images get `loading="lazy"` and `decoding="async"`. - The primary image accepts the `priority` prop as an escape hatch — when true, do NOT set `loading="lazy"` on it (render it eager, since it may be an LCP candidate). Default (`priority` absent/false) can still be `loading="lazy"` OR eager, your call — but document the reasoning either way, since PLP tiles above the fold ARE LCP candidates per AGENTS.md's "LCP ≤2s p75 mobile" priority, and tiles below the fold should lazy-load. Since this component doesn't know its own position, defaulting to lazy with an opt-in `priority` escape hatch (rather than defaulting to eager) is the safer default — a caller that knows it's above the fold sets `priority`. - Aspect ratio comes from the RECIPE (`aspectRatio` CSS), not a fixed pixel height — the component/recipe must not contain a `288px`/`179px` literal anywhere. Root should be `width: '100%'`, matching the "the card is fluid" architecture decision recorded in the plan. - Hover-swap (`swapOnHover` + `hoverImage` both present): BOTH images exist in the DOM simultaneously; which one is visible is controlled by CSS (opacity/visibility) keyed off a hover selector in the RECIPE (`zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`), not by JS toggling a `display`/conditional-render. Gate this rule the same way as everywhere else in this build: `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`. **Prev/next arrows (desktop/hover-capable only):** - Native `

7	 * and that it is NOT floating dots; per-segment width/gap and the exact colour pairing are not

9	 * (documented below) rather than invented pixel-for-pixel guesses — same precedent as
10	 * zimmColourSwatchGroup's `pagination` part leaving an unconfirmed inter-button gap at the flex
11	 * default rather than inventing one.
12	 *
13	 * Two parts:
14	 *   - `root` — the full-width flex strip, exactly `--zimm-scale-025` (1px) tall.
15	 *   - `dot` — one equal-width segment per image (despite the part name, this renders as a
16	 *     rectangle in a hairline, not a circular dot — the name matches this component's
17	 *     already-agreed contract, not a literal shape description).
18	 */

20	  parts: ['root', 'dot'],
21	
22	  baseStyle: ({ isActive }: { isActive?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
23	    root: {
24	      display: 'flex',
25	      // Fluid, not a fixed Figma px width — matches the product card's own "fluid, not 288px"
26	      // rule: this strip always spans whatever width its image parent gives it, rather than
27	      // the specific 159.11px/99.44px bounding boxes the two sampled Figma variants happened
28	      // to measure at their own artboard widths.
29	      width: '100%',
30	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-025)', // 1px — the one dimension Figma confirms directly.
31	      // No confirmed inter-segment gap value in the export handed to this step — left at 0

2	
3	*Last updated: 2026-06-25*
4	
5	*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Search & Recommendations" (SPR), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Regional Storefronts" (REG), "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD).*
6	
7	*Status key: **Confirmed** = safe to implement. **Open** = do not implement; question noted.*
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Page Structure & Content
12	
13	### 1.1 Layout (SPR-01, SPR-02 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
14	- Dedicated category landing page; products displayed in a grid layout.
15	- "View more" pattern (not infinite scroll) loads additional products. The per-page count (currently 36) is handled in the FE — not configurable via BM (IC 2026-05-25).
16	
17	### 1.2 Editorial / SEO Content (SPR-03, SPR-04 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
18	- Editorial/SEO paragraph with a "read more" expand action (not collapsible — confirmed per 24.06 design review); positioned below YMAL / Recently Viewed (RJ note).
19	- Configurable title, description, and hero image per category page via Business Manager.
20	- Design TBC: hero image included in the page header; H1/description placement is exploring a discreet location or inline in page code.
21	
22	### 1.3 Inline Editorial Hero (SPR-64 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
23	- Optional editorial hero image rendered inline within the product grid (not in the page header).
24	- Optional headline and body text alongside the image; design may also include H1/H2 text elements.
25	- Configurable by business users in Business Manager.
26	- New feature introduced in Song UX redesigns.
27	
28	### 1.4 Inline Category Links (SPR-65, SPR-66 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
29	- Configurable set of inline category links displayed below the hero image and above the product grid.
30	- Links are contextual — an edit of subcategories (not all are shown).
31	- Business users define and prioritise which subcategories appear inline per page in Business Manager.
32	- Full category set remains accessible within the filtering panel.
33	
34	### 1.5 Business User Controls (SPR-07, SPR-08, SPR-09 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
35	- Business users can preview category and product states before publishing.
36	- Categories and products can be toggled online/offline in Business Manager.
37	- Category visibility can be scheduled in advance (seasonal/campaign automation).
38	
39	---
40	
41	## 2. Product Tile (SPR-10–SPR-18)
42	
43	### 2.1 Tile Content (SPR-10, SPR-11 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
44	- Each tile shows: product image, name, and price.
45	- Each colour variant is shown as a separate tile.
46	
47	### 2.2 Pricing Display (SPR-12 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
48	- Currency per storefront (REG-036, **Confirmed**).
49	- Markdown/sale pricing on PLP tiles uses "Was/Now" format — original retail price and reduced sale price both shown.
50	- "Was" price is retained if the price changes again after being put on sale (REG-042, **Confirmed**) — see regional.md for detail.
51	
52	### 2.3 View Toggle (SPR-05 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
53	- Model view / Item view toggle switches all tiles between model photos and flat/item photos.
54	- Toggle selection persists across pagination and filter changes within the session.
55	- Note: model view may be removed pending design (RJ note) — implement toggle but allow it to be hidden via config.
56	
57	### 2.4 Hover Behaviour (SPR-13 — Confirmed 2026-05-08, subject to design)
58	- Desktop hover alternates between the model and flat/item image stored per tile.
59	- New designs may instead play a video of the model view on hover, and/or use an image slider on the PLP (RJ note).
60	- Final image vs video behaviour is design-dependent — confirm with design before implementing the video variant.
61	
62	### 2.5 Wishlist (SPR-14, SPR-15 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
63	- Save-to-wishlist icon on each product tile.
64	- Tapping the wishlist icon prompts size selection so entries are saved at SKU/size level.
65	- Full wishlist spec: see account.md, Wishlist section.
66	
67	### 2.6 Product Badges (SPR-16 — Confirmed 2026-05-08; PRD-005, PRD-006 — Confirmed)
68	- Badge taxonomy (defined in pdp.md section 3): **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** (PRD-005).
69	- Badges driven by configurable product attributes in Business Manager; multiple badges per product supported with a defined display priority/hierarchy when more than one applies (PRD-006). Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change").
70	- Badges are display-only on PLP tiles. Clickable badges that filter the PLP to that category are a NEW unsigned request — not confirmed; see Open Items (PRD-005). Do not implement.
71	- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005, PRD-006).*
72	
73	### 2.7 Quick Add to Bag (SPR-17 — Confirmed 2026-05-08, subject to design)
74	- Enables adding a product to cart without navigating to the PDP.
75	- The customer must **select a size before** the item is added to the bag (mirrors the wishlist size-selection pattern in §2.5) (SPR-17).
76	- When the item is out of stock the add-to-cart icon is **greyed out/disabled**, surfacing **'coming soon' / 'back in soon'** as alt/hover text instead of an add action (SPR-17). Cross-ref the out-of-stock availability rules in §3.
77	- Final UI is design-dependent.
78	
79	### 2.8 Merchandising Rules (SPR-18 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
80	- Business-user-controlled merchandising: manual curation, rules-based ordering, and scheduled updates.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 3. Availability & Stock Display (CAI-024–CAI-031 — Confirmed)
85	
86	- **OUT OF STOCK** shown on tile when all sizes are at or below buffer threshold.
87	- Business users can suppress OOS products from PLP entirely (toggle in Business Manager).
88	- Low-stock indicator shown at size level (no quantity number) — applies within a size selector if present.
89	- Buffer stock thresholds and availability display rules: see cart.md section 5.
90	
91	### 3.1 OOS Sort/Suppression (SPR-31 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
92	- OOS products are automatically demoted or suppressed within category and search results — no manual intervention required.
93	- Per-category override is supported via BM configuration (IC 2026-05-25) — some categories may retain OOS items higher in the grid for collection presentation.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 4. VIC / Exclusive Products (CAI-046–CAI-047 — Confirmed)
98	
99	- Exclusive/VIP products are not shown to ineligible customer groups on PLP or in search.
100	- VIC Exclusive badge shown on tile for eligible customers.
101	- Full VIC/exclusive product spec: see cart.md section 8.
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 5. Filters & Facets (SPR-19–SPR-32, SPR-68)
106	
107	### 5.1 Faceted Navigation (SPR-19 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
108	- Driven by product attributes defined in the SFCC catalogue.
109	- Configurable by business users in Business Manager at:
110	  - **Global level** — colours, size.
111	  - **Category level** — e.g. sleeve length for Dresses.
112	
113	### 5.2 Filter Logic (SPR-20, SPR-21, SPR-22 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
114	- Facet values that would return zero results when combined with already-applied filters are hidden.
115	- OR logic within a facet (e.g. Red OR Blue); AND logic across facets (e.g. Colour AND Size).
116	- Multi-select within a facet group is supported.
117	
118	### 5.3 Global & Category-Specific Facets (SPR-23, SPR-24, SPR-25 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)
119	- Global category filters: colour, size, material, availability.
120	- Category-specific facets (e.g. sleeve length) configurable per category in Business Manager.
